routes.description: Establish human flourishing as the shared comparative standard, then show that secular humanism better advances it through revisable evidence-based inquiry, contextual moral reasoning, and consequence-sensitive conflict resolution.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the secular framework supplies defensible methods for rational and moral decisions, connects those methods to human welfare, answers the foundational objections, and supports comparative superiority over Christian authority.

motionBridge.description: Connect secular humanism's goals, methods, and practical consequences to superior achievement of the motion's four stated domains.

centralBridges.description: Justify human flourishing and empirically informed human interests as a meaningful common standard for comparing the worldviews.
Show how revisability, logical testing, experience, and independent corroboration support rational decisions despite acknowledged fallibility.
Explain how objective, value-relative and context-sensitive assessment can guide conduct by its effects on human welfare.
Demonstrate how secular principles address cooperation, equality, peace, and doctrinal conflict more reliably than unsupported authority claims.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend the position that using logic and reliable inquiry need not include an ultimate account of their origin or a guarantee of certainty.
Explain why comparative claims about flourishing should depend on evidenced human consequences rather than unverified supernatural rewards.

routes.description: Establish that comparative superiority requires a coherent objective foundation, then argue that Christianity grounds rational intelligibility, moral obligation, and human flourishing while secular humanism cannot justify its own standards.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if secular humanism's accounts of cognition, scientific inference, and welfare-based ethics are shown to be circular or self-undermining, while Christian foundations provide a coherent basis for reason, morality, and flourishing.

motionBridge.description: Connect Christianity's claimed foundations for intelligibility, ethics, and flourishing to superiority across the motion's comparative domains.

centralBridges.description: Require a worldview-neutral, non-question-begging standard capable of supporting a genuine judgment of comparative superiority.
Show why physically caused cognition and intersubjective checking require an account of reliable access to mind-independent logical truth.
Ground logic, scientific presuppositions, and nature's uniformity in God's rational character and the design of human minds.
Ground moral duties in divine character and revelation while explaining why chosen goals and consequences cannot justify themselves.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect biblical instructions concerning love of God and neighbor to a substantive Christian account of human flourishing.
Establish freedom from self-refutation as a threshold condition for trusting a worldview's conclusions about welfare and conduct.

sections.title: Comparative Standard and the Meaning of Flourishing
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether human welfare supplies a shared basis for comparison or whether superiority requires a further objective and worldview-neutral standard.

sections.title: Cognition, Logical Inference, and Epistemic Reliability
sections.rationale: The dispute over physical cognition, fallibility, correspondence, and independent corroboration bears directly on each worldview's capacity for rational decision-making.

sections.title: Foundations of Logic, Science, and Intelligibility
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether practical reliance on logic and science is sufficient or whether their presuppositions require a specifically Christian metaphysical foundation.

sections.title: Moral Standards, Consequences, and Context
sections.rationale: The competing accounts of objective revelation and welfare-based contextual judgment form the central clash over how moral claims are justified and applied.

sections.title: Practical Outcomes, Cooperation, and Conflict Resolution
sections.rationale: This issue connects the foundational disputes to equality, peace, scriptural disagreement, present-life welfare, and the practical resolution of human conflicts.
